audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir while the content layer and the packet both read Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Hwei/Skill/Hwei/Hwei — the page answered 'who wins Level 1' two different ways.
audit.why: Vladimir has no ranged answer to Hwei's paints before Sanguine Pool, and his kit is a sustained-fight kit rather than a duelling one; the two agreeing layers plus a 52.57% win rate over 2549 games support the Hwei-favoured chart.
audit.corrected: Full layer moved onto the content chart: Hwei 1-3 and 4-5, Skill at 6, Hwei at first item and two items.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text never named a real Vladimir cooldown or the anti-heal timing that decides the matchup.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s and Transfusion 9/7.9/6.8/5.7/4.6s with no resource cost, so every window is defined by those two numbers plus Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Spikes now key off Pool's 28s rank-1 cooldown, Transfusion's free 9s poke, and buying Grievous Wounds before his second item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither the untargetable window nor the healing was stated as a mechanic — only referred to vaguely as 'his pattern'.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool makes him untargetable for 2 seconds, which eats Spiraling Despair's detonation and any queued paint; Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal him, so chip damage without Grievous Wounds does nothing over an extended trade.
audit.corrected: Bait Sanguine Pool first, commit in the 26s it is down, and have anti-heal online before you try to kill him through Hemoplague.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit in it (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT), and dosFull[2].d called Sanguine Pool a 'fifteen-second' cooldown.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 and never shorter than 16s.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into both fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings under unrelated titles; dontsFull[0].d used 'they' for a male enemy.
audit.why: Lint flagged both bleeds; champ-gender.js has Vladimir male.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to match their titles and pronouns corrected.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. It governs your forward steps. - E fear paint spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Sanguine Pool: 28s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — two seconds untargetable eats a whole commit, so bait it and detonate inside the downtime. - Transfusion costs no mana and is back every 9s, so chip without Grievous Wounds heals straight off him.

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling through your detonation, healing the chip back off Transfusion, and closing to 625 for Hemoplague.

edits.before: Standing mid-cast-animation inside his engage range with the fear already spent — every assassin and fighter in the pool is waiting for exactly that frame.
edits.after: Committing your signature while Sanguine Pool is up — he sinks for two seconds, the detonation hits nothing, and he walks out healed by Transfusion.

edits.before: Carry through range — no mid pool champion paints a teamfight from further away; your R + QQ decides objectives before they start.
edits.after: Carry by outranging the heal — he must reach 600 for Transfusion and 625 for Hemoplague, and everything you own lands further out.

edits.before: If Vladimir opens the score, reset expectations and respect Sanguine Pool doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with QA clears and stay relevant through max-range poke.
edits.after: If Vladimir opens the score, stop trading into a full Transfusion and buy Grievous Wounds a component early. After a second kill, farm with QA clears and only step up when Sanguine Pool is visibly spent.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Lead with a cheap paint so he pools early — the 28s cooldown at rank 1 is the whole kill window you get.

edits.before: QQ his last-hit, weave any second spell for the mark, detonate, and reset to max range — two-spell trades he answers only by overextending.

edits.before: Vladimir burns Sanguine Pool on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.

edits.before: That’s Vladimir’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.

notes: packet.suspectNames flagged 'Use Sanguine Pool' in wants.foe[1] as a probable wrong name — it is a FALSE POSITIVE; Sanguine Pool is the real W name in the kit, so that field was left alone.
